statement: The pinned WiiBrew Rumble and Output Report common information sections identify output report 0x10 as direct rumble control, but also describe bit 0 in the first payload byte of every output report as the current rumble on/off request. Consequently a host keeping rumble active must preserve that bit whenever it sends an unrelated output; clearing the bit even during an LED, memory or other request can stop rumble unintentionally. This is the documented report protocol, not verification of actual motor activation.
